- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon when sentiment is positive (especially >0.27) — model tends to overreact to bullish sentiment.
- Underestimate when sentiment is negative or near-zero (especially <0.1) — model misses downside risk or fails to adjust for bearish signals.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes — model often peaks too early and then underperforms, especially if sentiment was high before the spike.
- Exhibit mean reversion bias — model frequently forecasts a “correct” price after a sharp move, but fails to account for momentum or volatility clustering.
- Lag in response to sentiment shifts — model reacts slowly to sentiment changes, especially when sentiment turns negative mid-horizon.
- Overweight recent history in short-term forecasts — model overfits to recent price movements, ignoring sentiment-driven structural shifts.
- Underweight sentiment in long-term forecasts — model ignores sentiment trends when projecting 30-day horizons, leading to persistent bias.
- Correct for “sentiment echo” — if sentiment is consistently positive, model should not over-forecast upward; if sentiment is negative, avoid over-forecasting downward.
